analyses.title: Top pain points among Gen Z respondents
analyses.question: What do Gen Z survey respondents name as their single top frustration?
caveats: Each respondent names one top frustration; counts are out of the Gen Z respondents matched.
analyses.summary: Fit inconsistency is the most common top frustration, named by 108 of 400 Gen Z respondents, ahead of price versus value at 72.

interpretation.text: Fit, sizing and durability together outweigh price as the frustrations Gen Z respondents name first.

analyses.title: Fit and personalization pain points, Gen Z vs 28+
analyses.question: How often is fit inconsistency or lack of personalization the top frustration, for Gen Z and for customers aged 28 and older?
analyses.summary: Fit inconsistency is the top frustration for 27.0% of Gen Z respondents against 19.0% of older respondents; lack of personalization is named by 7.0% and 4.0%.

interpretation.text: Fit friction is broader and sharper among Gen Z respondents, while personalization is a minority concern in both groups.

analyses.title: Promoters and detractors, Gen Z vs 28+
analyses.question: What share of each cohort are promoters (9-10) and detractors (0-6)?
caveats: NPS is promoters minus detractors, computed from these shares.
analyses.summary: Among Gen Z respondents 40.0% are promoters and 18.0% are detractors, against 58.0% and 9.0% among older respondents.

interpretation.text: Gen Z respondents are both less enthusiastic and more critical, so the gap is not explained by one group alone.

analyses.title: Fit and personalization pain points by segment
analyses.question: Which customer segments most often name fit inconsistency, or lack of personalization, as their top frustration?
caveats: All survey respondents, all ages; segments differ in size.
analyses.summary: Value Seekers name fit inconsistency (28.8%) and lack of personalization (10.6%) more often than any other segment; Established Active name fit least often (19.0%).

interpretation.text: Fit friction is concentrated in the younger, value-minded segments rather than spread evenly.

analyses.title: Price sensitivity, Gen Z vs 28+
analyses.question: What is the average self-rated price sensitivity (1-5) for each cohort?
caveats: Stated sensitivity on a five point scale, not observed price response.
analyses.summary: Gen Z respondents rate their price sensitivity 3.90 on average, against 3.20 for older respondents.

interpretation.text: A premium-priced proposition faces a more price-sensitive Gen Z audience than older customers.

analyses.title: Price sensitivity by segment
analyses.question: Which customer segments rate themselves most price sensitive?
caveats: Stated sensitivity on a five point scale, not observed price response.
analyses.summary: Campus Competitors are the most price-sensitive segment at 4.02 on average and Established Active the least at 3.20.

analyses.title: Q3 2026 returns by reason
analyses.question: Why were products returned in Q3 2026?
caveats: Return counts only: some per-product reason shares in the returns sheet do not add up, so shares are not shown.
analyses.summary: Changed mind is the largest single return reason (7,301 returns), but fit running large (5,085) and fit running small (4,449) together exceed it.

interpretation.text: Fit-related returns are a larger cost pool than any other controllable reason, including durability.

analyses.title: Products with the highest return rates
analyses.question: Which products have the highest return rates this fiscal year to date?
analyses.summary: The highest return rate this year to date is 16.8%, followed by 14.6% and 13.8%; the table names each product.

interpretation.text: The two products with the highest return rates are the same footwear lines named in durability and fit-related evidence.

analyses.title: Gen Z channel scorecard, September 2026
analyses.question: How do channels compare for Gen Z shoppers on conversion, order value and returns in September 2026?
caveats: A single month; monthly return rates should not be averaged across months.
analyses.summary: Stores convert Gen Z shoppers at 18.2%, far above Marketplace at 4.0%, Social Shop at 3.4% and Brand Site at 2.2%.

interpretation.text: Online channels bring reach but convert Gen Z shoppers much less efficiently than stores.

analyses.title: Social Shop net sales, Q1 vs Q2 2026
analyses.question: How much did Social Shop net sales grow from January-March to April-June 2026?
analyses.summary: Social Shop net sales rose from $886,762 in Jan-Mar to $2,146,098 in Apr-Jun.

interpretation.text: Social Shop is growing quickly from a small base.
